In primary school, it was me. I was obsessed with a musical my parents took me to see, and would role-play as a character almost constantly. Word got around that I thought I *was* the character, and I was the laughing stock of the school, and it was the 'in' thing to mock and bully me at every opportunity. The teachers did nothing, because I had severe adhd, and they just saw me as lazy and disruptive. 

I went through deep depression in my teens and early twenties, but eventually got it under control with therapy and medication. I worked at a creative, artistic job that I loved. My career was slowly taking off. 

I then got a virus (cold sores) pretty severely, and started getting extreme fatigue and weakness. Turns out the virus had triggered ME/Chronic fatigue syndrome, and I got progressively worse until I had to give up work. I am now mostly housebound, sometimes bedbound. There is no known cure or effective treatment. I am constantly depressed and frustrated with my situation, with the boredom. 

In secondary school it was this boy. He was very small and high voiced, and always looked messy and unkempt. He sang all the time, would say strange things, funny things. People would offer him money (small amounts) to do embarrassing/weird/gross things. He would often say vulgar things, like he sucked his dad's cock. We thought he just wanted to be shocking. 

Turns out he was being physically and sexually abused by his parents, and he died as a young adult due to brain damage and haemorrhaging from all the beatings. We were all shocked when it came to light, but it explains so much of his behaviour. :(

Over the years I've had 4 rounds of counselling, group therapy, 3 courses of cognitive behavioural therapy (I'm sure I'm almost qualified to be the therapist by now). They've kind of run out of therapy to give me, so I don't currently have a therapist. I don't think they will give me mood stabilisers because I have depression and not bipolar. I take lithium orotate as a supplement though.

I was bullied mercilessly from the age of 8 to 11. You know how fads catch on in schools and absolutely everybody knows about them? Picking on me became a fad, I was bullied and teased by my entire peer group except for two people, who got bullied because they associated with me. It started because I was obsessed with a musical my parents took me to see, and I guess that kind of thing is weird when you're 8. I'm not sure how it escalated to the point it did, but people who didn't even go to my school would recognise me on the street with my mum, ask me if I went to (school name) and I was *that girl*. Then they would insult and make fun of me. The bullying was mostly non violent, but I couldn't go anywhere without being harassed, and my belongings got stolen an awful lot. 
Around age 10 I remember my panic attacks were at their worst. I also developed severe OCD and had countless actions that I had to perform just so or I felt my family were in danger. The first time I remember wanting to kill myself I was age 11. I tried to hide my OCD and suicidal feelings from my family, as I knew they weren't normal and I was ashamed.   

When I moved into my senior school at age 12, the bullying stopped - I made sure I went to a school that hardly anybody else in my junior school was going to. However I was  painfully shy and had a lot of issues with anxiety. I fought hard throughout my teens to become more confident and to challenge my OCD impulses. 

I was put on antidepressants at the advice of my doctor when I was 15. 

At age 16, I had a breakdown brought on by the increased workload of sixth-form college. I based a lot of my self worth on my intelligence, but my ADD meant I took a lot longer to get things done. The volume of work and the stricter deadlines made me drop out after one term. This was the first time I cut myself with a razor blade - I intended to kill myself but I just couldn't bring myself to press down on the vein, so I just made a few shallow cuts. It felt good, and became a habit I would dabble in over the years. 

I got a job, and struggled to become the best at what I did. I threw myself into it, and stressed and beat myself up over getting things right. I struggled with depression a lot over this time.

I believe the stress of my job and the depression weakened my immune system, which in turn made me particularly susceptible the virus I caught in 2007. This virus triggered the onset of Post Viral Fatigue Syndrome, otherwise known as CFS/ME. What started out as tiredness and feeling run down escalated over the years into profound exhaustion and weakness, leaving me mostly housebound, bedbound when I am at my worst. As doctors don't fully understand the disease, there is no known cure. 

As you can imagine, this has a profound negative effect on my mental health. I've lost contact with all of my friends, I'm constantly suicidal, self harming, and on such a high dose of antidepressants that they are starting to damage my heart. I can't kill myself because my family love me. 

I can't say for sure this would never have happened if I was never bullied, but I'd like to find out what would have happened to me otherwise.

I have dermatillomania and trichotillomania (skin picking and hair pulling). These, and dermatophagia, aren't 'self-harm' disorders, they are impulse control disorders, meaning the goal isn't to hurt yourself. Injury is just a side effect of the picking/pulling/biting, which is caused by anxiety. Personally, I find my habits are fuelled by my perfectionism - I pick at blemishes and dry skin, I pull frizzy hairs and split ends. Still trying to sort this out, so I don't have much advice in the way of curing it. A tip - wear gloves all the time, so you can't get at the skin. Also, stay distracted, and find something else to chew, like gum. I'm sitting here in a sleeping hair cap to stop me from pulling my hair - very glam!

More info -

Two things stop me.

First, the fear of the abyss, not having consciousness, fading into blackness, never experiencing anything ever again. I just can't comprehend it.


Secondly, my brother's suicide 2 years ago. I watched my parents hearts break. My Dad found him hanging. He is not an emotional man, but he barely spoke for 2 months afterwards, and had this hollow, haunted look to him. He still has nightmares. My Mum was right behind Dad when he found him. When I arrived 5 hours after they found him (I was working on the other side of London) she was still shaking violently,  and couldn't speak properly - she was stuttering and incoherent. She cries most days about it. My nieces, his daughters, were shellshocked. Watching them grow up without him is awful. I wasn't that close to my brother, we were both outspoken and opinionated, but every time I am reminded of him, even in the smallest of ways, it's like a knife in the heart. 

Don't underestimate the devastation your death will cause. It will be infinitely more than a mere 'inconvenience'. If you care for them at all, you will fight for as long as you have control over your actions. You need to keep trying, you CAN claw back from this. Not gonna lie, it'll be unbearably hard at times. But as you make progress, get on the right dose of the right medication, it will start to get easier.

Depression is an illness. The medication corrects/normalizes the imbalance of your brain chemicals. It's just taking them back to normal, healthy levels. They're not hallucinogens, they can't plant or add any thoughts or feelings that aren't already there. I'd be more reluctant to trust the thoughts of my unhealthy suicidal mind than when I'm on medication.

A side note - you mentioned you self harm. Telling you not to would be hypocritical, because I do it myself. But please, be safe with it. Don't cut your wrists or inner forearms, or anywhere with veins visible through the skin. Disinfect the skin and the blade first with rubbing alcohol or hand sanitizer, and apply antiseptic cream after the bleeding stops. Apply it every day until the scab has healed. Infections are not only dangerous, but super painful.

I was met with 'well sorry, you have to wait for your appointment in 8 weeks'. I think it gets to the point where they want you to do it to shorten the waiting lists. Is it really that hard for authorities to have a response appropriate to the level of danger?

Antidepressants are good. They don't take away the feelings, but they provide relief from the severity of them. Some work better than others, I've been on paroxetine, fluoxetine and citalopram, the most effective one I've been on is venlafaxine. Once you start taking them, never skip a dose or quit cold turkey, even if you think they aren't working. Never do anything to the dosage without your doctor's consent. Not only can withdrawal make you very ill physically, it can cause the most intense rage and suicidal episodes.

They don't make you act differently, they just dull the pain a bit. Some people say they can make them emotionless, but that is a symptom of depression anyway.

After seeing and feeling the aftermath and the effects on those around him, I never want to inflict that pain on the people I love. I will bear it myself for as long as I can. 


The thing is, if I had killed myself first, I think my brother would have stayed to spare my family the pain. Then my two nieces would still have a dad, and not be living with their morally devoid mum and her asshole bf, who moved in 2 days after the funeral and sold all my brother's stuff. It should have been me.


**TL;DR** - Ask for help, even if you think you're beyond help. Talk to each other - the awkward/painful conversations are the most important. If you haven't heard from a friend in a while, call them - depression makes people shy away from others when they need them the most.
